# tetrastack **the libraries, references, and rejections behind everything i build for the web** [stack](#the-stack) · [taste](taste.md) · [voice](voice.md) · [perf](perf.md) · [rejected](rejected.md) · [skill](SKILL.md)
every entry here has shipped in a real project ([parc](https://parc.rev.school), [tetraslam.world](https://tetraslam.world), tetravoice, and others) or earned its place in my [taste collection](https://tetraslam.world/taste). it's written for agents first: point one at this repo and it builds the way i would. ## use it ask your agent: > build me a ____. use github.com/tetraslam/tetrastack for the stack and taste. to make it permanent, install it as a skill. it then loads on its own whenever a web project starts: ```sh git clone https://github.com/tetraslam/tetrastack ~/Programming/tetrastack ln -s ~/Programming/tetrastack ~/.agents/skills/tetrastack ``` the skill also handles the other direction. "add torph to tetrastack, it's the right way to morph text" files the entry in the right place, then commits and pushes it. ## the stack | layer | default picks | | --- | --- | | [app](stack/app.md) | next 16 · vite outside next · pnpm · tailwind 4 · biome · zod · nuqs | | [backend](stack/backend.md) | convex · convex-helpers rls · better auth · resend + react email · an errors table instead of sentry | | [ai](stack/ai.md) | ai sdk + gateway · ai elements · streamdown · opentraces with outcomes · firecrawl | | [ui](stack/ui.md) | shadcn on base ui · phosphor · cmdk · sonner · tiptap · dnd-kit · use-stick-to-bottom | | [motion](stack/motion.md) | motion · torph · paper shaders · vgpu · dither · dot matrix · conway | | [content](stack/content.md) | @pierre/diffs · @pierre/trees · shiki · katex · mermaid · unified | | [ship](stack/ship.md) | vitest · convex-test · react doctor · vercel + analytics | each entry says what it is, when to reach for it, what to watch out for, and where it shipped. ## hardware [hardware/](hardware/README.md) is the same idea for physical things: printed parts, circuit boards, firmware and robots. it's a starting list, and nothing in it has shipped yet. ## taste [taste.md](taste.md) holds the constants every project keeps (hierarchy first, every state designed, nothing shifts), a dozen directions to choose from (warm paper, live dither, title card, kinetic menu, lens, painterly, hardware specimen, raw text, and more), the bar (three elements from my own work, down to the edge cases), and the references behind it all: pierre, gwern, nous, prime intellect, palladium, oxide, natural, persona 5, evangelion, kyoto animation, and more. every project picks its own look in a [brief](brief.md) before any ui code, and studies it from the primary sources in [directions/](directions/), so nothing converges on one house style. ## effective perf [perf.md](perf.md): perf is what the user feels. prefetch everything one click away, server-render the real first paint, no skeletons on fast loads, nothing moves, writes are optimistic. agent interfaces make the wait legible instead. references: mcmaster-carr, nextfaster, linear's sync engine, deepseek r1. ## voice [voice.md](voice.md): how the words sound, chosen per project like the look is. it holds the rules every voice keeps and a list of voices in [voices/](voices/), each written from real samples. the first one is [discord](voices/discord.md), which is how i type. ## rejected [rejected.md](rejected.md) lists tools i've retired (clerk, radix, lucide, prisma) and things i won't use (sentry, langfuse, fake-hacker monospace). an agent learns as much from these as from the picks. ## # directions

one file per direction from [taste.md](../taste.md#directions). each lists primary sources (the real thing: archives, original works, frame galleries, the designer's own writing) and, under **on the web**, live sites that use the style with real craft. both say what an interface should take from each.

the bar for **on the web** is diffs.com, pierre.computer, oxide.computer, teenage.engineering. one excellent example beats three mediocre ones, and "none at the bar yet" is an honest answer.

agents: after picking a direction in the brief, open its file, visit and screenshot every source, and build from those, not from memory. `status: draft` means unreviewed, so treat it as a lead and verify. `status: approved` means curated.

links only. no copyrighted images live in this repo.

## format

```md
---
direction: <name>
status: draft | approved
---

# <name>

<one line: what it is, what it fits>

## sources
- [<what it is>](<url>): <what to take, concretely>

## on the web
- [<site>](<url>): <what to take>

## avoid
<the generic cliché agents produce from memory>
```

# acid graphics

chrome, warped type, rave-flyer energy, neon on black, liquid 3d forms. fits music, events, culture, and launches that should feel loud.

## sources
- [collector’s archive of original 1989–2000s rave flyers, organized into regional and thematic collections](https://www.flickr.com/photos/villalobosjayse/collections/72157626196424298): study stretched display lettering, dense event information, synthetic imagery, and abrupt palette clashes. Preserve the distinction between expressive headline artwork and compact, readable logistical text.
- [Bráulio Amado’s own portfolio, including Good Room posters and record artwork](https://badbadbadbad.com/): study lettering that becomes illustration, uncomfortable scale changes, and deliberately limited but abrasive color combinations. Give each composition one dominant distortion rather than applying a universal glitch filter.
- [Jonathan Castro Alejos’s own visual-work archive and portfolio website](https://jonathancastro.pe): study the collision of organic texture, digitally manipulated surfaces, and precise typography. Keep navigation simple enough to expose the work; let the imagery supply instability.

## on the web
- [Dekmantel, the electronic-music festival's official site](https://dekmantelfestival.com/): fluorescent yellow-green lettering, purple fields, distorted insignia, and degraded imagery carry the rave identity while navigation stays compact and readable. keep expressive artwork separate from dependable ticketing.

## avoid
lime green plus black, chrome blobs, and a distorted font pasted onto an otherwise ordinary SaaS layout.

# art deco

geometric ornament, gold on deep color, symmetric fans and stepped forms, elegant display type. fits luxury, hospitality, finance with glamour.

## sources
the warm, restrained kind: san francisco lobbies and towers, old gold and bronze against cream stone. not black-and-gold glam.

- [the Shell Building, from its restoration architect](https://www.hellermanus.com/shell-building): gold-toned elevator doors, pale marble, ornamental grilles, directory lettering, shell motifs in the floor. the strongest warm-material reference: pale stone becomes surfaces, metal becomes fine borders and labels.
- [140 New Montgomery, the owner's gallery](https://140nm.com/gallery/): the Pacific Telephone building. narrow vertical proportions, setbacks, bronze details, geometric lobby ceiling.
- [450 Sutter, the owner's history](https://450sutter.com/about): Mayan-inspired terra-cotta spandrels and bronze-finished ceiling relief. take the geometric relief and finely drawn lettering; its darker marble is the exception to the cream palette.
- [Aquatic Park's murals and mosaics, from the National Park Service](https://www.nps.gov/safr/learn/historyculture/artists-of-aquatic-park.htm): streamline moderne by the water. muted colors, simplified contours, gold and silver leaf used selectively.
- [the Golden Gate Bridge's deco details, from the bridge district](https://www.goldengate.org/exhibits/art-deco-on-a-grand-scale): stepped brackets, chevrons, fluting, staggered pylon tops. use it for geometry, not palette.
- [the Paramount Theatre in Oakland, its restoration](https://www.paramountoakland.org/about/restoration): vertical rhythm and grille patterns. the whole theatre is lusher than the target, so take parts, not the room.
- [I. Magnin, Oakland, 1951 photograph](https://calisphere.org/item/24f954c997ed88cf44d8693a5039bfd0/): facade rhythm, lettering, and cornice proportions (monochrome, so not color).
- [Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann's Fuseaux cabinet, ca. 1925, at the Met](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/487425): intricate pattern inside a simple, carefully proportioned enclosure. translate slender supports against a solid body into fine rules framing generous content.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. The Edmon, 140 New Montgomery's site, and Léna all fall short. architectural character alone doesn't make an excellent website.

## avoid
A black-and-gold Gatsby template with sunbursts, excessive letterspacing, and indiscriminate geometric trim.

# bauhaus

primary colors, circles, squares, and triangles, type as construction. fits education, tools, anything about form and function.

## sources
- [Joost Schmidt’s poster for the 1923 Bauhaus exhibition](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/6235): Construct a composition from interlocking circles, bars, and a shared diagonal. Let lettering participate in that geometry while keeping functional interface copy horizontal.
- [Herbert Bayer’s 1923 Bauhaus exhibition postcard](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/189328): Study how compact typography and geometric forms occupy the same small field. Use changes of direction and weight selectively, with clear boundaries between display lettering and supporting information.
- [Bayer’s wall-painting study for the Weimar Bauhaus stairwell, 1923](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/178202): Use colored planes to articulate actual spatial divisions. In a UI, assign color to navigation zones, section boundaries, or functional groups rather than floating decorative shapes.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. nothing found has both the style and the craft. the Bauhaus-Archiv site has relevant typography but isn't an exceptional web reference.

## avoid
Random red circles, yellow triangles, and blue squares scattered over an otherwise conventional landing page.

# bento grid

content in tidy tiles of different sizes, each one a self-contained idea. fits overviews, dashboards, product pages with many facets.

## sources
- [An archived copy of Bento’s own team page, built with its mixed-size content widgets](https://web.archive.org/web/20240228122720/https://bento.me/aboutus): Mix portraits, social links, and editorial blocks using a small family of tile sizes. Keep gutters and corner treatment consistent while allowing content to determine each tile’s composition.
- [Apple’s product presentation, combining large product imagery with compact feature and specification modules](https://www.apple.com/mac-mini/): Let major product claims occupy larger areas and subordinate specifications occupy smaller ones. Alternate photography, short text, and numerical emphasis without giving every module equal visual weight.
- [Microsoft’s illustrated explanation of the Windows 8 Start screen, 2012](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/askperf/windows-8--windows-server-2012-start-screen-and-user-interface-part-1/375111): Study modular square and double-width tiles, explicit groups, and information visible before opening an application.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. the strongest current examples (Raycast, Linear) are the generic-dark-devtool attractor. Apple's product pages, in the sources above, remain the reference.

## avoid
Arbitrary rounded rectangles containing identical icon-heading-paragraph stacks, with empty oversized tiles added only to complete a mosaic.

# blueprint / technical drawing

white line on blue, dimension lines, callouts, orthographic views. fits engineering, hardware, robotics, anything that explains how it's built.

## sources
- [Charles Bulfinch’s wooden-truss bridge plan and elevation, ca. 1810–1832, with downloadable scans](https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/95860747/): Align multiple views of the same object and distinguish outline, internal structure, and annotation. Use the empty space around drawings to make relationships legible.
- [AISC’s *Structural Steel Bridge Shop Drawings* manual, containing specimen drawing sheets](https://www.aisc.org/media/hd0atw1y/b903_sbdh_chapter3.pdf): Study the drawing specimens’ title blocks, detail identifiers, dimension chains, and separated notes. Translate these into consistent metadata panels, labeled diagrams, and explicit cross-references.
- [Original Chrysler Building electrical-plan blueprint, 1929](https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2020630454/): Use the sheet’s overall organization as a reference: several related plans within one bounded document, with reserved annotation areas.

## on the web
- [Podium, a control-panel builder whose identity is built from real panel schematics: fine linework on charcoal, cream and yellow fields](https://www.podiumautomation.com/): derive the graphic system from the thing being engineered, and keep detailed technical imagery separate from simple readable panels. the [case study](https://www.zypsy.com/work/podium) shows the link between the equipment and the site.

## avoid
A blue graph-paper background covered with meaningless measurements, crosshairs, and decorative engineering labels.

# braun functionalism

calm off-white and gray, one signal color, precise controls, nothing extra. fits utilities and devices.

## sources
- [Rams’s ten principles, published by Vitsœ and illustrated with original Braun and Vitsœ products](https://www.vitsoe.com/us/about/good-design): Make controls and information explain themselves. Use restrained navigation, plainly labeled content, and generous separation; remove decoration that competes with the user’s task.
- [Braun T3 pocket radio, 1958, by Dieter Rams and Hochschule für Gestaltung Ulm](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/4134): Organize the surface into a repeated field and one dominant control. Use consistent spacing, quiet neutral materials, and clear differences between passive information and manipulation.
- [Braun ET55 calculator, 1980, by Dieter Rams and Dietrich Lubs](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/3697): Group controls by function within a regular matrix. Use selective color and tonal contrast to distinguish special actions; keep labels short and their placement consistent.

## on the web
- [Teenage Engineering, a hardware identity carried onto the web: custom pictograms, compact labeling, precise product imagery, purposeful accent colors](https://teenage.engineering/): make the interface feel designed by the people who designed the object, carrying its labeling, proportions, and visual logic across both.
- [Analogue, carefully art-directed hardware presentation with restrained navigation, controlled typography, and exceptional product staging](https://www.analogue.co/): give the product visual authority. a quiet interface still has character through proportion, image composition, and type.

## avoid
Beige neumorphic cards, ornamental speaker grilles, and an orange button added without a functional reason.

# constructivism

diagonals, red and black, photomontage, bold sans type as propaganda. fits announcements, movements, activist or community products.

## sources
- [El Lissitzky’s *Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge*, 1920, in the Art Institute’s exhibition archive](https://archive.artic.edu/tass/203887): Make geometry communicate a specific action: penetration, direction, opposition. Align display text with the dominant vector; reserve strong red for the active force.
- [Aleksandr Rodchenko’s design for Mayakovsky’s *About This. To Her and to Me*, 1923](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/16012): Combine sharply cropped photography with large typographic blocks. Use deliberate scale discontinuities and hard-edged montage instead of softly blended imagery.
- [Rodchenko’s cover for *Novyi LEF*, issue 1, 1928](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/8217): Treat the publication name, issue number, and supporting text as distinct compositional units. Build a reusable editorial system from bold type, rectangular divisions, and concentrated accent color.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. the leads were unavailable, archived, or conventional sites with an old constructivist case study.

## avoid
Red-and-black propaganda wallpaper, fake Cyrillic, and diagonals applied equally to headings, paragraphs, and controls.

# editorial grandeur

seriousness, restraint, hope. fits long-form and ideas.

## sources
- [Palladium’s magazine homepage, with essay headlines, artwork, excerpts, and author/date metadata](https://www.palladiummag.com/): Give titles and images enough space to establish intellectual weight. Keep supporting metadata visibly subordinate, and use long-form editorial hierarchy rather than sales-page headings.
- [Stripe Press’s catalog and book presentations](https://press.stripe.com/): Treat covers as substantial designed objects. Give each title its own color identity while maintaining disciplined typography and generous separation between books, descriptions, and endorsements.
- [St Bride Library’s digitized copy of Bodoni’s *Manuale tipografico*](https://archive.org/details/20771_202210): Study high-contrast letterforms, centered specimen compositions, and the amount of unprinted space surrounding type. Reserve delicate display faces for sufficiently large sizes.

## on the web
- [Palladium, a magazine about governance and society](https://www.palladiummag.com/): a monumental serif masthead, generous opening whitespace, restrained navigation. hierarchy gives the writing institutional weight with no ornamental interface.
- [Emergence, a multimedia publication on ecology, culture, and spirituality](https://emergencemagazine.org/): immersive imagery and discreet editorial controls make a contemplative reading environment. borrow the drastic scale difference between the story's visual world and the interface around it.
- [Works in Progress, a magazine about scientific, technological, and economic progress](https://worksinprogress.co/): fine rules, warm paper tones, and precise publication metadata frame expressive commissioned artwork. a disciplined editorial frame for serious material that still feels warm.

## avoid
Beige backgrounds, oversized italic serif slogans, and arbitrary “EST. 1894” details masquerading as cultural authority.

# editorial / magazine

a strong grid, big headlines, pull quotes, columns, image and type in conversation. fits writing, publications, long reads.

## sources
- [The Paris Review’s publication site, integrating stories, quarterly issues, interviews, and archival material](https://www.theparisreview.org/): Distinguish content types through recurring labels and hierarchy. Keep bylines, excerpts, and issue information available without letting metadata overpower titles.
- [It’s Nice That’s visual-culture publication](https://www.itsnicethat.com/): Use image-led modules, varied story prominence, and clear category navigation to support browsing. Let commissioned imagery provide color instead of giving every article an artificial colored card.
- [Emigre’s archive of its 69 magazine issues](https://www.emigre.com/Magazine): Study purposeful departures from the grid, expressive type scale, and issue-to-issue variation. Experimental spreads work because relationships between text and image are composed, not randomly disrupted.

## on the web
- [Aeon, a publication on philosophy, science, psychology, and culture](https://aeon.co/): strong serif headlines, restrained metadata, and decisive lead-story sizing set a clear reading order. not every article is an equal card.
- [The Pudding, interactive visual essays](https://pudding.cool/): each story has its own artwork, inside a recognizable archive system with numbered entries and illustrated navigation. stable publication structure, individual story identities.
- [It's Nice That, contemporary creativity and visual culture](https://www.itsnicethat.com/): large lead stories, smaller supporting items, color-coded sections. density and image scale vary while captions and metadata stay consistent.

## avoid
A giant masthead above an endless uniform card grid, or decorative pull quotes that interrupt reading without adding meaning.

# evangelion / nerv

emergency orange and red on black, hexagonal panels, condensed warning type, a heavy mincho for titles, system readouts. fits monitoring, ops, anything with alarms. see also title card.

## sources
- [frame-by-frame original episode sequence showing emergency displays, illuminated status panels, and graphs](https://wiki.evageeks.org/FGC:Episode_02_Scene_07a): inspect cuts 243 onward for repeated warning cells and the contrast between huge emergency labels and compact telemetry. Use repetition to communicate escalation, with color changes tied to actual states.
- [EvaWiki's MAGI article, with original frames of the MAGI displays](https://wiki.evageeks.org/Magi): study the three-part system diagram, angular boundaries, large node names, and subordinate technical labels. Give topology meaning: each region should represent a real subsystem or decision.
- [original Jet Alone control-room frames, including password entry, errors, and danger indicators](https://wiki.evageeks.org/FGC:Episode_07_Scene_09): compare ordinary data display with the abrupt takeover by a large error message. Use restrained operational screens so exceptional warnings can genuinely dominate.
- [official NERV Disaster Prevention app website, showing a real information-dense warning interface](https://nerv.app/en/): study legible maps, explicit severity labels, large countdowns, and selective alert colors. This is a useful practical counterweight to fictional screens: urgency must improve recognition.

## on the web
- the nerv console (private, `~/Programming/nerv/console` on this machine): a trading-agent monitor built from the sources above. the 遅延 overdue state, a MAGI vote answering "does it need me", a time-down tape, hold-to-halt. studied from frames, not themed.

otherwise none at the bar yet. the live libraries and fan dashboards lean on hazard stripes, scanlines, and decorative telemetry.

## avoid
orange hexagons, meaningless numbers, and “WARNING” labels scattered across every surface regardless of state.

# frutiger aero / y2k

glossy bubbles, sky and water, aqua glass, optimistic tech. fits consumer apps that should feel bright and hopeful.

## sources
- [original Mac OS X 10.0.4 screenshots documenting early Aqua](https://guidebookgallery.org/screenshots/macosx100): study luminous rounded controls, fine pinstriped surfaces, translucent materials, and distinct pressed/selected states. Concentrate gloss on interactive objects rather than applying the same gradient everywhere.
- [functioning Aero-styled website and image collection covering period interfaces, advertising, wallpapers, and hardware](https://frutigeraeroarchive.org/): examine glossy navigation, pictorial icons, blue/green color relationships, and the gallery’s original UI examples. Notice how photographic nature imagery and manufactured surfaces coexist without eliminating readable content panels.
- [curated collection of original Y2K-era visual artifacts, with an expandable gallery](https://cari.institute/aesthetics/y2k-aesthetic): study metallic and translucent objects, rounded technological forms, synthetic color, and compact futuristic lettering. Use this to distinguish Y2K materiality from later Aero’s airy, nature-oriented presentation.

## on the web
- [Webamp, a working browser Winamp with playlists, equalizer, skins, and visualizations](https://webamp.org/): dense metallic panels, luminous readouts, tiny controls whose states stay distinct. borrow the coordinated panel system and the visualization area, not the original control sizes.
- [7.css, a Windows 7 component library with live demos](https://khang-nd.github.io/7.css/): translucent window frames, glossy controls, inset fields, and layered borders. material treatment distinguishes draggable frames, editable areas, and actionable controls.

## avoid
merging chrome Y2K lettering, Vista glass, vaporwave grids, and floating dolphins into one indiscriminate nostalgia theme.

# fui

thin lines, scanning grids, telemetry, targeting overlays, sci-fi readouts. fits monitoring, robotics, real-time data.

## sources
- [GMUNK’s original *Oblivion* interface-design archive, with screen graphics, process imagery, and motion reels](https://gmunk.com/OBLIVION-GFX): Build screens on a consistent dot grid; use thin structural lines, compact labels, and bright color only for operational distinctions. Give maps, diagnostics, and targeting views the same underlying geometry.
- [Territory Studio’s production archive for *Blade Runner 2049*, including development reels and finished interfaces](https://territorystudio.com/project/blade-runner-2049/): Differentiate systems through material behavior: degraded optical imagery, chunky utilitarian readouts, or restrained corporate displays. Texture should communicate the equipment’s age and purpose.
- [Documented screenshot archive covering *Alien* interfaces and their reuse in later films](https://scifiinterfaces.com/category/alien-franchise/alien-1979/?order=asc): Study bounded CRT displays, low-color wireframes, large status changes, and physical controls surrounding screens. Use clear operating modes rather than filling every available pixel.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. Kaspersky's cybermap has the vocabulary but not the craft; SpaceX's docking simulator is promising but unassessed.

## avoid
Cyan concentric circles, meaningless telemetry, perpetual scanning animations, and glowing borders on every panel.

# game boy / 8-bit

a four-shade palette, a pixel grid, bitmap fonts, chunky sprites. fits games, toys, nostalgic or very constrained interfaces.

## sources
- [Nintendo’s original Game Boy Tetris listing, with gameplay screenshots and trailer](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Game-Boy/TETRIS--275924.html): study the strongly bounded playfield, narrow statistics column, tile-based borders, and differentiation through patterns rather than many colors. Keep pixel sizes and alignment consistent.
- [Nintendo’s Pokémon Red page, with original-game screenshots](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Game-Boy/Pokemon-Red-Version-266109.html): study boxed dialogue, small directional selection markers, sparse battle layouts, and compact status bars. Build hierarchy through placement and framing before increasing font size.
- [live specimen page for an 8-bit-style web component library](https://nostalgic-css.github.io/NES.css/): inspect stepped corners, hard-edged borders, pixel shadows, and actual form controls. Useful for translating raster-era grammar into web components; its colorful NES vocabulary is distinct from monochrome Game Boy.
- [ModRetro's Chromatic, a modern Game Boy Color-compatible handheld](https://modretro.com/collections/chromatic-consoles): the hardware itself is the reference: translucent and solid shells, a real LCD playfield framed by a bezel label and a segmented trim stripe. take the bezel framing and the bright, toy-like product color against deep studio backdrops.
- [PICO-8, Lexaloffle's fantasy console](https://www.lexaloffle.com/pico-8.php): a fixed 16-color palette, 128×128 screen, and a 4×6 font, with the editor, sprite sheet, and music tracker in the same tiny pixel UI. take a hard palette constraint and one pixel grid shared by tools and content; its [cartridge BBS](https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?cat=7) shows thousands of games living inside it.

## on the web
- [PICO-8, product site and playable showcase](https://www.lexaloffle.com/pico-8.php): cartridge thumbnails, pixel lettering, and a playable console in the middle make the limits tangible. a restricted palette and fixed visual units, with real interaction carrying the nostalgia.
- [Playdate, Panic's crank handheld](https://play.date/): the yellow object stays central, the screen is enlarged to show real games, and specs are plainly labeled. a modern pixel-screen product presented with confidence, not nostalgia.

## avoid
a pixel font on rounded modern cards, mixed pixel scales, and CRT scanlines imposed on an LCD-derived style.

# greco-futurism

sky, stone, open space, foundations. fits products that must earn trust.

## sources
note: tnkr.ai no longer shows the classical treatment this direction was named from. these are adjacent sources, not one established movement.

- [The Art Institute’s high-resolution reproduction of Piranesi’s *Interior view of the Pantheon*, 1768](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/64586/interior-view-of-the-pantheon-from-views-of-rome): Study monumental scale established by tiny figures, repeated architectural bays, and an enormous uninterrupted central volume. Translate that into deliberate empty space and strong proportional relationships, not scattered column clip art.
- [The fabricator’s project gallery for Calatrava’s Athens Olympic structures](https://www.metka.gr/en/activities/infrastructure-projects/certified-buildings/olympic-athletics-complex-of-athens): Use repeated slender structural members, sweeping curves, and coherent white surfaces to connect classical procession with contemporary engineering.
- [The Classical Futurist’s own publication archive](https://www.classicalfuturist.com/archive): Study how conventional editorial typography, restrained navigation, and historically grounded imagery can carry the classical association without turning the interface into a temple.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. the product sites investigated no longer show the classical direction, and the design-system experiments are generic.

## avoid
A marble bust floating above purple gradients, faux-Greek lettering, and AI-generated temples substituted for proportion and composition.

# hand-drawn sketch

wobbly lines, marker fills, whiteboard energy. fits brainstorming, early-stage tools, explanations.

## sources
- [Rough.js’s original illustrated specimen page, demonstrating sketch primitives and fill treatments](https://roughjs.com/): Control roughness, stroke weight, hachure angle, and fill spacing independently. Preserve recognizable geometry beneath the irregular outlines.
- [The working Excalidraw whiteboard application](https://excalidraw.com/): Keep application chrome quiet and readable while the drawing surface carries the sketch character. Use a limited palette, familiar diagram shapes, and generous canvas space.
- [Wired Elements’ live hand-drawn UI component showcase](https://wiredjs.com/): Study how rough outlines coexist with recognizable buttons, inputs, sliders, and selection states. Apply irregularity to rendering without making control boundaries or behavior ambiguous.

## on the web

# transit signage

strict color coding, bold sans labels, lines and stops, arrows. fits navigation, systems maps, routing and status.

## sources
- [Publisher’s reproduction of Vignelli and Noorda’s 1970 NYCTA manual, with photographs and scanned spreads](https://standardsmanual.com/products/nyctacompactedition): Treat arrows, route symbols, text baselines, and padding as one measured system. Repeat consistent horizontal sign bands and reserve route colors for identification.
- [MoMA’s collection record and image of the original NYCTA Graphics Standards Manual, dated 1966–70](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/89303): Study the manual’s own information hierarchy: strong headings, tightly organized specifications, and diagrams that explain relationships without decoration.
- [Transport for London’s official directory of graphics, signage, interchange, and related design standards](https://tfl.gov.uk/info-for/business-and-advertisers/design-standards): Follow the linked standards for symbol clearances, lettering hierarchy, and consistent directional information. Separate destination, direction, and service identity rather than mixing them into one label.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. the Port Authority's wayfinding manual site is a plain document site; the system lives in its PDFs.

## avoid
Random Helvetica, decorative subway lines, and colored circles that do not identify stable destinations or categories.

# tufte data-ink

maximum data, minimum chrome, small multiples, sparklines, labels instead of legends. fits analytics, research, anything numbers-first.

## sources
- [Tufte’s official book page, with original sample spreads from the foundational statistical-graphics book](https://www.edwardtufte.com/book/the-visual-display-of-quantitative-information/): Let data marks carry the visual weight; subordinate rules and axes. Use comparable scales and small multiples instead of decorative chart containers.
- [Tufte’s official *Beautiful Evidence* page with sample spreads](https://www.edwardtufte.com/book/beautiful-evidence/): Place images, quantitative evidence, and explanation together. Use precise annotations near their referents rather than separating “insights” into distant cards.
- [Working web specimen translating Tufte’s book typography and marginalia into responsive HTML](https://edwardtufte.github.io/tufte-css/): Study the main-column/sidenote proportions, ET Book typography, near-white background, and figures that selectively extend beyond the text column. Collapse marginalia deliberately on narrow screens.

## on the web
- [Gwern's site, a long-form reading system](https://gwern.net/): scholarly typography, sidenotes, recursive link previews. the main argument stays readable while supporting material lives in place.
- [Red Blob Games, interactive technical explanations](https://www.redblobgames.com/): diagrams and prose form one teaching interface. controls sit beside the thing they change, and visual encodings stay consistent between diagrams.

## avoid
A beige serif blog labeled “Tufte,” with oversized whitespace and the actual evidence hidden behind tabs.

# ukiyo-e / woodblock

flat color planes, bold outlines, patterned water and sky, a carved line. fits storytelling, culture, and slow, beautiful products.

## sources
- [The Met’s Hokusai *Under the Wave off Kanagawa*, ca. 1830–32](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/45434): Use a few strongly separated color masses, dark contour lines, and large asymmetrical shapes. Borrow the dramatic scale contrast and framing of negative space rather than reproducing the wave.
- [Hiroshige’s *Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake*, 1857](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/55433): Study the steep diagonal bridge against broad horizontal fields, localized tonal gradation, and fine rain lines. Keep texture directional and subordinate to the main silhouette.
- [Hiroshige’s *Sudden Shower in Shōno*, ca. 1833–34](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/36967): Layer dark foreground shapes against pale distant forms; use diagonals to direct reading. Keep title cartouches discrete and rectangular instead of scattering ornamental lettering.
- [Hiroshige’s *Mishima: Morning Mist*, ca. 1833–34](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/10926): fog drawn by removing the key-block line. Far forms become flat grey silhouettes, each paler than the one before, with no outline, while near figures keep full line and color.
- [Hiroshige’s *Autumn Moon over Tama River*, ca. 1837–38](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/47805): the moon as an unoutlined pale disc in a blue bokashi, low mist bands over the far shore, water as flat pale ribbons.
- [Hiroshige’s *Kanbara: Evening Snow*, ca. 1833–34](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/25613): night without black. A sumi bokashi from the top, everything else held in two or three greys.
- [Hiroshige’s *Ryōgoku Bridge and the Great Riverbank*, 1856](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/34277): beni bokashi on the horizon at dusk, a bridge in perspective with piers as rhythmic dark verticals.
- [Kawase Hasui’s *Misty Moonlight at Matsue*, 1924](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/2587) (shin-hanga, in copyright): night light done with one lit window, lit cloud edges, broken reflections. Study it for changing light; the edo prints rarely show the same place at different hours.

## learned in practice
- kiri (live golden gate fog): the same view printed as weather states is the genre's native form (tōkaidō morning mist, sudden shower, evening snow). Treat each color as a block: flat fill, pigment pooling at block edges, woodgrain in large fills, washi fiber through every ink. Put the key line only on near forms.
- Draw weather as disappearance, not as a shape. Every attempt to draw fog's own surface (stacked billow rows, domes, scalloped undersides) read as stickers to an outside critic; what worked was one seamless sheet with a few broad billows at its far edge, long horizontal reserves wiped away at their lower edge, and what stands inside it greyed to a flat ghost with its key line gone.
- Missing data has a medium-native state: print only the key block, a proof on bare paper, so it can't pass for clear weather.

## on the web
none at the bar yet. showing ukiyo-e artworks on a page doesn't make a woodblock interface.

## avoid
A Great Wave background, red sun, cherry blossoms, and faux-Japanese display type pasted onto ordinary cards.

# rejected

what not to reach for. read this before adding anything that isn't in [the stack](README.md#the-stack). if you add something anyway, say why.

## retired

used before and replaced. existing projects can keep these. new projects shouldn't.

| was | now | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| clerk | better auth | better auth covers every case, including heavy multi-role apps, without a vendor dashboard |
| radix | base ui | shadcn's default since july 2026, built by the same people |
| lucide | phosphor | weights and fill states let icons match the type |
| framer-motion | motion | same library, new package |
| eslint + prettier | biome | one fast tool |
| prisma + postgres | convex | one backend for data, search, files, jobs, and realtime |
| npm, yarn | pnpm | |
| newsreader | source serif 4 | preferred the reading texture |
| jetbrains mono | commit mono | quieter, and reads less like an editor screenshot |

## never

| what | why |
| --- | --- |
| sentry and other external error services | heavy. write errors to a convex table and show them in an admin tab |
| langfuse and most llm observability tools | bad trace uis. raindrop is the exception worth learning from. store opentraces in convex |
| cloudflare | won't use |
| php | slopware |
| unmaintained packages | slopware, however good they once were |
| raw html where shadcn has a component | inconsistent and inaccessible |
| inline styling everywhere | componentize, and pull values from tokens |
| fake-hacker monospace aesthetics | mono as a costume. it works when the content really is text for machines (pierre) or the product's voice (mintlify); otherwise be technical through clear hierarchy (oxide) |
| stock shadcn gray with no theme | the default theme is a starting point, not a design |
| gradient blobs, glassmorphism for its own sake, emoji in ui | generic ai-template look |
| "agents" without tools | an agent can always call tools and take multiple steps |
| google fonts over the network | self-host with fontsource |

# motion

animation, shaders, and generative texture. this layer does the most to make something feel alive instead of templated.

### [motion](https://motion.dev)
layout transitions, presence, gestures. load features lazily (`LazyMotion` + `domAnimation`) so the bundle only pays for what's used.

### [torph](https://torph.lochie.me)
dependency-free text morphing. the right way to animate text that changes in place: labels, counters, status lines.
- **shipped in**: parc, tetravoice, rev-website, fashion

### [paper shaders](https://shaders.paper.design)
shader components for react (`@paper-design/shaders-react`). best on regions with no text over them, and best when they respond to interaction, like the dithering warp in delve-onsite's upload area that changes color and speeds up on hover.
- **shipped in**: tetravoice, tetrachat, re-zero, delve-onsite, rev-website

### [vgpu](https://vgpu.sh)
webgpu surfaces and effects. share one low-power device across the app, import it lazily, and fall back cleanly when there's no webgpu.
- **shipped in**: parc

### [dither-plugin](https://dither.floriankiem.com)
a tailwind plugin for dither effects, in mono or color, over images, gradients, and animations.
- **shipped in**: parc, tetraslamworld

### [dot matrix](https://dotmatrix.zzzzshawn.cloud)
dot-matrix loader animations, compatible with shadcn. use it in place of a stock spinner.

### [conway](https://rankdim.github.io/conway/)
game of life embeds (`@rankdim/conway`). good patterns need structure, a decent speed, steady novelty, and evenly spread clusters. the palette matters as much as the pattern.

## to build

### ink reveal
paint bleeding in to reveal an image or surface, extracted from the [david whyte experience](https://davidwhyte.com/experience/) so it works anywhere.
- **mechanism**: a mask that thresholds noise against progress (`smoothstep(p - edge, p, fbm(uv * scale) + bias(uv))`). darken the pigment along the edge band the way watercolor dries, and multiply in paper grain.
- **progress sources**: time (on mount or when it enters the viewport), scroll position, pointer (local progress that falls off with distance from the cursor), or a value you control.
- **knobs**: duration and easing, noise scale and octaves, edge width and darkness, origin and direction (`bias`), grain amount, reveal or conceal.
- **runtime**: a small fragment shader on vgpu with a webgl2 fallback, like parc's field. a css `mask-image` with svg `feTurbulence` could serve as a no-gpu fallback.
- **reduced motion**: show the final state.

## contextual

- kuwahara pass ([painterly shaders](https://blog.maximeheckel.com/posts/on-crafting-painterly-shaders/)): post-processing that turns any rendered scene or image painterly. r3f-friendly.
- [three](https://threejs.org) + [react-three-fiber](https://r3f.docs.pmnd.rs): real 3d scenes (tetraslamworld's illustrated terrace). reach for paper shaders or vgpu first.

# taste

references for calibration, not templates. don't overindex and don't underindex: work out *why* each one works, then build something that's yours. never lift a reference's signature move (marked **signature** below where it's tempting). take the principle behind it and find this product's own version. open the source and look at it (with screenshots if you're an agent) before borrowing from it.

the full collection, with images, lives at [tetraslam.world/taste](https://tetraslam.world/taste) ([markdown](https://tetraslam.world/taste.md)). entries below link to it.

## constants

these hold in every project, whatever it looks like.

- **hierarchy before decoration.** on every screen and every row, decide what the reader needs first. give that the weight and let metadata recede (smaller, quieter, or on demand). no row repeats a label the layout already implies.
- **the main artifact leads.** whatever people came to read or use (a trace, a document, a conversation) is the hero, in its natural order. don't hoist summaries, final answers, or overviews above it, and don't dim the parts that carry meaning by default.
- **severity is honest.** loudness matches what actually needs the reader. an alarm fires only when they must act; noise, stale notes, and recovered errors stay quiet. a ui that cries wolf has failed.
- **show the present.** anything that monitors something live says what time it is, whether the thing is alive, and when it next acts. data is live or labeled with its age; never show a stale number as if it were current.
- **every state is designed.** rest, hover, focus, active, loading, empty, error, and success.
- **nothing shifts, nothing is lost.** no layout shift, and focus and scroll return to where they were. see [perf](perf.md).
- **transitions, not snaps.** anything that opens, closes, grows, or swaps transitions from its measured size on the project's curves. instant beats animated only when there's nothing to transition. a flicker or snap costs more perceived speed than a 200ms transition.
- **say less.** no subtitle under every item, no status pills that don't change a decision, no metadata the reader didn't come for. extra info goes on hover or on demand.
- **motion has a purpose.** each project names its own curves and durations and uses them consistently, and reduced motion is respected.
- **identity fits the product.** a social app, a devtool, and a reading site should not share a look. devtools are dense, calm, and legible.
- **copy talks like a person.** lowercase and warm, unless the direction calls for another voice. the voice is chosen per project from [voice](voice.md), the same way the look is.
- **type**: inter for ui and commit mono for code and numbers by default. the reading and display faces are chosen in the brief. source serif 4 and shippori mincho b1 are favorites, not obligations.

## directions

every direction has a file in [directions/](directions/) with primary sources to study before designing.

the look is chosen per project, in a [brief](brief.md) written before any ui code. a direction is studied, not themed: before using one, collect primary sources (real frames, real pages, real objects, not what the style looks like in general), note what makes each work, and build from those. naming a style and then drawing on the average of the internet produces generic slop: chamfered cards, tracked uppercase micro-labels, and a hex wallpaper are not evangelion. the agent picks whatever suits the product best: a direction from this list, a style that isn't listed, or a deliberate blend. the list is a starting range, not a menu. the order here means nothing, and none of them is the default. never start from another project's css or tokens, including parc's.

- **warm paper** (parc): warm off-white surfaces stepped a few percent apart, hover as ink overlays, one accent (ember) that means alive or yours, and a dither field on surfaces that take input. fits places people live in daily: social, messaging, notes.
- **live dither** (delve-onsite): dark, grainy, with a shader that breathes on the one surface that matters and reacts to every state. fits single-purpose tools with one hero interaction.
- **illustrated serif** (tetraslam.world): serif typography, an illustration with a sense of place, considered light and dark. fits personal and editorial sites.
- **title card** (evangelion): black and white, a heavy mincho set huge, stretched or squeezed, in broken stacked layouts, cut in hard. fits launches, story-driven pages, and moments that should feel like an event.
- **kinetic menu** (persona 5): a palette of two or three colors at full contrast, angled shapes, cut-out lettering, and a transition with personality on every action, while staying readable. fits games, playful consumer apps, anything where navigating is the experience.
- **lens** (kyoto animation): soft light, bloom, depth of field, focus pulls as transitions, pastel color, attention to tiny states. fits reflective, personal, and media products.
- **painterly** (kuwahara, oil, ink reveal): paint and watercolor surfaces, often as an atmospheric backdrop behind a precise technical artifact, as on prime intellect's inference page. fits research, creative tools, and anything that should feel made by hand.
- **hardware specimen** (oxide): the look of physical machines, with textured controls, cell grids, and technical clarity without hacker costume. fits infrastructure and serious devtools.
- **raw text** (pierre): the content is the design. markdown, mono, a cursor. fits products for machines and agents.
- **greco-futurism** (tnkr): sky, stone, open space, foundations. fits products that must earn trust.
- **editorial grandeur** (palladium): seriousness, restraint, hope. fits long-form and ideas.
- **native material** (ghostty): the product renders its own pitch in its own medium (ascii in a terminal, a live trace in a trace viewer). fits any product with a strong medium.
- **neobrutalism** ([neobrutalism.dev](https://neobrutalism.dev)): flat saturated color, thick black borders, hard offset shadows, unapologetic type. fits playful tools and anything that should feel direct.
- **skeuomorphism**: real materials and objects (leather, paper, knobs, glass) rendered so controls look like what they do. fits instruments, creative tools, anything tactile.
- **bento grid**: content in tidy tiles of different sizes, each one a self-contained idea. fits overviews, dashboards, product pages with many facets.
- **editorial / magazine**: a strong grid, big headlines, pull quotes, columns, image and type in conversation. fits writing, publications, long reads.
- **scrapbook**: collage, tape, torn paper, handwriting, stickers, things pinned at angles. fits personal, social, memory and collection apps.
- **acid graphics**: chrome, warped type, rave-flyer energy, neon on black, liquid 3d forms. fits music, events, culture, and launches that should feel loud.
- **evangelion / nerv**: emergency orange and red on black, warning bands that take over the screen, condensed warning type, a heavy mincho for titles, system readouts. fits monitoring, ops, anything with alarms. see also title card.
- **art deco**: the warm, restrained kind: san francisco lobbies, old gold and bronze against cream stone, stepped geometry, fine metal grilles and lettering. not black-and-gold glam. fits hospitality, finance, and anything that should feel established and elegant.
- **game boy / 8-bit**: a four-shade palette, a pixel grid, bitmap fonts, chunky sprites. fits games, toys, nostalgic or very constrained interfaces.
- **swiss / international typographic**: a rigorous grid, sans-serif type, asymmetric layout, flat color, lots of white space. fits information-heavy products that need clarity.
- **bauhaus**: primary colors, circles, squares, and triangles, type as construction. fits education, tools, anything about form and function.
- **constructivism**: diagonals, red and black, photomontage, bold sans type as propaganda. fits announcements, movements, activist or community products.
- **memphis**: squiggles, terrazzo, clashing pastels and primaries, playful geometry. fits consumer fun, kids, creative play.
- **risograph / zine**: two or three spot inks, misregistration, grain, photocopied texture, hand-made layouts. fits indie publishing, communities, small-batch creative work.
- **blueprint / technical drawing**: white line on blue, dimension lines, callouts, orthographic views. fits engineering, hardware, robotics, anything that explains how it's built.
- **braun functionalism** (dieter rams): calm off-white and gray, one signal color, precise controls, nothing extra. fits utilities and devices.
- **fui** (film hud): thin lines, scanning grids, telemetry, targeting overlays, sci-fi readouts. fits monitoring, robotics, real-time data.
- **retro os** (classic mac, windows 95): windows, bevels, pixel icons, a menu bar. fits playful tools, personal sites, nostalgia.
- **frutiger aero / y2k**: glossy bubbles, sky and water, aqua glass, optimistic tech. fits consumer apps that should feel bright and hopeful.
- **tufte data-ink**: maximum data, minimum chrome, small multiples, sparklines, labels instead of legends. fits analytics, research, anything numbers-first.
- **transit signage** (vignelli, wayfinding): strict color coding, bold sans labels, lines and stops, arrows. fits navigation, systems maps, routing and status.
- **ukiyo-e / woodblock**: flat color planes, bold outlines, patterned water and sky, a carved line. fits storytelling, culture, and slow, beautiful products.
- **museum archive**: specimen labels, catalog numbers, plates, captions, archival paper. fits collections, research, libraries, taste pages.
- **receipt / thermal print**: narrow mono columns, dotted rules, timestamps, totals. fits logs, transactions, small utilities with personality.
- **solarpunk**: lush green, warm sun, art nouveau curves, optimistic ecology. fits climate, community, and hopeful futures.
- **illuminated manuscript**: drop caps, marginalia, ornament, gold leaf, rubrication. fits reading, scholarship, anything meant to feel precious.
- **hand-drawn sketch** (rough.js): wobbly lines, marker fills, whiteboard energy. fits brainstorming, early-stage tools, explanations.

## the bar

three elements from my own work that show how much detail is possible. hold anything new to this standard, then use the details below as a checklist. the bar is the level of care, not the look: don't copy these elements' colors or shapes into other products. link to them for mechanisms (state machines, focus restore, render-on-change), not for style.

### the upload field · delve-onsite
the drop zone is a live paper-shaders `Dithering` warp, not a static gradient. on hover or drag it brightens from dormant deep blue (`#0f1a24`) to forest green (`#1a4a3a`), speeds up from 0.2 to 0.6, and the shader layer scales to 1.05 over 700ms while the icon ring scales and tints over 500ms. the submit button fills with a wash from left to right on hover. every state of the surface has its own motion, and they all share one ease-out. [source](https://github.com/tetraslam/delve-onsite/blob/master/frontend/src/components/file-upload.tsx)

### the field · parc
the same idea grown into a material: an ordered-dither (8×8 bayer) fbm shader that appears only on surfaces that take something from you. it has five states (rest, compose, intent, receive, work), each with an energy level from 0 to 1. energy eases toward the current state's level with a 0.22s time constant, the color shifts from cold to warm with it, and a glow follows the cursor.
- it runs on webgpu through vgpu, falls back to webgl2, and caps the pixel ratio at 2.
- it renders only while energy is changing or the texture is moving, and pauses offscreen.
- under reduced motion it snaps to the target and holds still.
- dropping files anywhere on the page puts every receiving field into `receive`.

### the composer · parc
press `n` anywhere:
- if the composer is on screen, it opens in place. if not, it remembers your scroll position and focused element, scrolls the composer to just under the top bar, and opens once scrolling ends (with a 700ms fallback). its field shows `intent` on the way there.
- opening morphs the editor's min/max height on the morph curve (32px to 84px, capped at 45vh). nothing else on the page jumps.
- `escape` closes it and takes you back where you were, focus included. clicking away closes it without scrolling. `⌘enter` posts, the composer closes, and the new post appears in place.
- the edge cases are handled: reduced motion jumps instead of scrolling, a window blur (file chooser, other app) doesn't count as leaving, iOS safari's late blur on tapping "post" doesn't collapse the button before the click lands, and an open mention menu or gif picker gets escape and enter first.

## art direction references

the sources behind several directions. painting styles carried onto the screen. study the technique, then use it as one element on a surface, not as the whole site.

### [on crafting painterly shaders](https://blog.maximeheckel.com/posts/on-crafting-painterly-shaders/) · [entry](https://tetraslam.world/taste/on-crafting-painterly-shaders)
- maxime heckel builds paint, watercolor, and aquarelle looks in webgl from first principles, with a runnable sandbox at every step.
- the kuwahara filter (and its anisotropic version) does most of the work: an edge-preserving blur that turns detail into brushy patches of color.
- what makes it read as paint: no fine texture or normal detail, preserved edges, quantized color.

### [oil paint brush](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/MtKcDG) · [entry](https://tetraslam.world/taste/oil-paint-brush)
- flockaroo's shader repaints live video as oil, stroke by stroke. the strokes follow the image's structure instead of blurring it.
- see also his notebook drawings and ballpoint sketch shaders.

### ink reveal · [david whyte experience](https://davidwhyte.com/experience/)
paint bleeding in to reveal an image. the effect is worth extracting from the site into a standalone, configurable component (see [motion](stack/motion.md#to-build)).

### persona 5 (game ui)
- red, black, and white only. lettering cut out like a ransom note, menus set at angles, jagged shapes, and a transition with personality on every action.
- for all that chaos, text stays high-contrast and the current choice is always obvious. the bar for "stylish but readable".
- the ui is the identity: menus, calling cards, and splash screens all speak the same language as the story.
- [game ui database](https://www.gameuidatabase.com) for more.

### evangelion title cards
- matisse eb, an ultra-bold mincho serif, in white on black: set huge, stretched or squeezed to fill the frame, stacked in l-shaped and broken layouts, and cut in hard on the beat.
- typography with timing. it's hideaki anno's signature and carries into his later work (shin godzilla, shin ultraman).

### kyoto animation (violet evergarden, hyouka, sound! euphonium)
- they animate as if through a real camera lens: bokeh, rack focus, light leaks, a little chromatic aberration, and soft pastel light.
- small physical details carry the emotion: hands, feet, a sleeve, a glance.
- on the web: depth of field and focus pulls as transitions (blur what's no longer in focus instead of fading it), soft light and bloom instead of drop shadows, and attention to tiny states.
